raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both Study A (Cooper et al., 2021) and Study B (Behnke et al., 2020) are companion systematic scoping reviews produced by the same UNC Water Institute team from the exact same master literature search and screening pipeline (10,324 peer-reviewed records searched up to 12 October 2017 + 100 grey literature records searched up to 6 January 2018; 6,949 unique records screened; 1,125 full texts assessed; 307 total eligible publications). From that shared 307-publication pool, the team partitioned publications into emergency (n = 104), transitional (n = 88, analyzed in Study A), and protracted (n = 213, analyzed in Study B) displacement phases, explicitly noting in Study B Table 3 that the phase counts sum to 405 rather than 307 because multi-phase publications were included in more than one review, and noting in Study A that only 28 of its 88 publications (32%) focused exclusively on the transitional phase. Consequently, up to 60 publications overlap across phases, and multiple specific primary studies—including those cited for legal/policy and institutional obstacles (e.g., Mohamed et al., 2014; UNICEF and Hydroconseil, 2017; Schuller and Levey, 2014; Tota-Maharaj, 2016; Toole and Waldman, 1990; Milton et al., 2017; Cronin et al., 2008, 2009)—are extracted and synthesized in both reviews.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Systematic scoping review of N = 88 publications (84 peer-reviewed, 4 grey literature; published 1946–2017 across 44 countries and the Occupied Palestinian Territories) addressing environmental health conditions, exposures, outcomes, obstacles, and recommendations in the transitional phase of forcible displacement (6 months to 2 years), drawn from a master pool of 307 eligible publications identified from searches on 12 October 2017 (peer-reviewed) and 6 January 2018 (grey literature). Only 28 of the 88 included publications focused exclusively on the transitional phase.
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Systematic scoping review of N = 213 publications (198 peer-reviewed, 15 grey literature; published 1946–2017 across 54 countries) addressing environmental health conditions, exposures, outcomes, obstacles, and recommendations in protracted forcible displacement (>2 years), drawn from the exact same master pool of 307 eligible publications (10,324 peer-reviewed records searched 23 September–12 October 2017 and 100 grey literature records searched 23 December 2017–6 January 2018; 6,949 screened; 1,125 full-text assessed).
